brief: A base with a bay bin in one half of its cell.

requirements.evidence: Three full bases: piece:0,-1,0;full, piece:1,-1,0;full and piece:-1,0,0;full. Together they surround the empty cell (0,0,0). The configurator offers bay trays only in an empty cell with bases on three sides, so it can't be done with one base.

requirements.requirement: Bay bin filling one half of the cell
requirements.evidence: bay:0#0,0#bay1 (hex-bin-bay-n-half-solid) is a half bay tray in the north half of cell (0,0,0). It is bolted to the three bases around it, and the south half is left open.
check_build: ok, meshClash clear. The only notes are info notes that open faces could take end caps.

finish.summary: Built three full bases around an empty cell and put a half bay tray (north half) in that cell. A bay can't share a cell with a base: the configurator refused a half base in the same cell (SITE_FILLED). Rule check and mesh-collision check are both clear.

lines.label: M6 x 20 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
